events.title: Continental Congress Approves the Articles of Confederation
events.description: After roughly sixteen months of debate, the Second Continental Congress approved the Articles of Confederation. The document set out a framework for a loose union of the American states in the middle of the Revolutionary War, and it was then sent to the states for ratification.
events.significance: The Articles became the first governing constitution of the United States. Their weaknesses later pushed leaders toward the drafting of the U.S. Constitution.

events.title: Brazil Becomes a Republic
events.description: A military coup led by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca deposed Emperor Pedro II and proclaimed a republic in Brazil. The monarchy ended without major bloodshed, and the imperial family went into exile.
events.significance: The coup ended Brazil's monarchy after nearly seven decades as an independent empire. The date is still celebrated as Republic Day, a national holiday.

events.title: The League of Nations Holds Its First Meeting
events.description: Delegates from 41 founding member states gathered in Geneva, Switzerland, for the first assembly of the League of Nations. The meeting came in the aftermath of World War I.
events.significance: The League was the first major international organization devoted to keeping peace. Its successes and failures shaped the creation of the United Nations after World War II.

events.title: The Soviet Space Shuttle Buran Flies
events.description: The Soviet Union launched its Buran orbiter on an unmanned mission. It completed two orbits and landed automatically, in a flight that was widely seen as a technical triumph.
events.significance: It was the only spaceflight Buran ever made. The program was later cancelled, but the flight showed that a reusable spacecraft could complete an entire mission under automated control.
